claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a lamellar FCC/B2 dual-phase microstructure.
The FCC constituent is relatively soft and the B2 constituent is relatively hard.
Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys is governed by a critical level of aluminum-induced chemical ordering.
Increasing aluminum above a critical threshold drives formation of the duplex lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure stabilizes the alloy under high-temperature, corrosive, radiation, and cryogenic service conditions.
Internal FCC/B2 phase boundaries impede defect propagation and thereby improve radiation tolerance.
The duplex phase arrangement slows oxide growth or corrosion and thereby improves environmental resistance.
A balanced distribution of soft FCC and hard B2 regions provides a favorable strength–ductility combination.
The FCC/B2 lamellar architecture helps retain strong mechanical properties at temperatures up to approximately 700 °C.
The soft/hard duplex architecture ensures cryogenic toughness.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can modify the duplex microstructure while retaining its lamellar character.
A slightly higher aluminum content than AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will produce a more pronounced and stable FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The optimized higher-aluminum alloy will retain phase integrity and mechanical properties better than the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 baseline across the proposed exposures.
Lower aluminum contents will fail to develop the FCC/B2 dual-phase structure.
Excessively high aluminum contents will produce excessive ordered phases and embrittlement.
The AlCoCrFeNi2.1 baseline exhibits a balanced combination of strength and ductility.
The AlCoCrFeNi2.1 baseline has established corrosion resistance.
Outside composition ranges near the eutectic point, single-phase solid solutions or other intermetallic compounds may dominate.
Outside the near-eutectic range, aluminum-induced ordering may cease to govern phase stability.
